assumptions: nodes is strictly increasing, matching x_0 < ... < x_n in the paper.
The parameter satisfies 0 < d <= n; d=0 is excluded because the paper credits that case to Berrut.
alpha < n and x lies strictly between nodes alpha and alpha+1.
p57Mu is equation (9) and p57Denominator is equation (10).

formal_statement.lean_header: theorem p57_t3_denominator_positive_between_nodes (nodes : Nat -> Real) (hmono : StrictMono nodes) (n d alpha : Nat) (x : Real) (hdpos : 0 < d) (hdn : d <= n) (halpha : alpha < n) (hxlo : nodes alpha < x) (hxhi : x < nodes (alpha + 1)) : 0 < p57Denominator nodes n d x
formal_statement.plain_language: Prove that the denominator in Theorem 1 is positive at every point strictly between two consecutive interpolation nodes when d is positive.

informal_proof: Split the denominator into the paper's left, middle, and right index blocks. The middle block is nonempty and termwise positive. Prove the product recurrence for consecutive mu terms and use it to show that each outer block, read away from the middle, is an alternating sum of nonincreasing magnitudes beginning positively. Pairing terms makes both tails nonnegative, so their sum with the positive middle block is positive.
informal_statement: Prove the interior-interval denominator positivity established in the proof of Theorem 1.

tier_rationale: The task requires proving a consecutive-product recurrence, constructing and proving a general finite alternating-sum lemma, translating both outer index blocks into alternating chains in opposite directions, managing truncated natural-number interval arithmetic, proving strict positivity of the middle block, and reassembling the three finite sums. The exact N proof has 257 physical lines and substantial indexed algebra rather than a short Mathlib import. The exact L mathematical proof is byte-identical and uses no NumStability declaration, establishing that the frozen library provides no speedup.
